_meta.source_notes: MSRPs (excluding destination) reflect the current US model year (MY2026 or MY2027) from manufacturer sites and automotive press as of September 2026. Ranges and efficiency are EPA figures from fueleconomy.gov unless a vehicle's notes say otherwise (some city/highway splits are derived from EPA MPGe). winter_range_mi is our derated WV estimate (~28% haircut). highway_range_mi is a realistic sustained 70-mph range: originally curated per model, and in the September 2026 refresh scaled from the new EPA range using each model's previous ratio (new models use ~80% of EPA, ~68% for Tesla). US/Canadian parts % is from NHTSA's MY2026 AALA report where listed. Spec fields not used by the calculator (home_max_kw, dcfc_peak_kw, cargo, towing) are informational; where a vehicle's notes don't vouch for them, treat them as unverified. Per-field confidence is documented at /state-of-the-data — refresh MSRPs quarterly.
_meta.status_values: current = sold new; final_year = production ended or last model year, new dealer inventory remains; discontinued = no longer sold new (kept for used-market shoppers and old shared links; msrp_usd is the last new price).
_meta.id_note: IDs are stable keys used in shareable calculator URLs. They do not track model year — an id ending in -2025 may describe a 2027 vehicle. Never rename an id.
_meta.curation_criteria: Selected for relevance to WV buyers: mix of price points, SUV/truck emphasis, AWD options, reliable dealer presence in WV or bordering states, PHEV options for range-anxious rural buyers, and several long-range luxury BEVs that also serve the used-market shopper.

vehicles.capability_note: Owner's manual figures for Premium 5-seat (Tesla's headline 76 cu ft is the total incl. frunk and sub-trunk). Towing requires tow package. Manual read via search excerpt (page blocks direct fetch). Sub-trunk: deep lower well under the cargo floor; Tesla gives no separate figure. The manual's 75.5 cu ft total = 71.4 rear + 4.1 frunk, so the rear figures already include the well. Accessory-vendor measurements put the well at about 2.1-2.9 cu ft (not official).
vehicles.notes: Dominant US EV SUV. Supercharger access. Verify pricing after recent Tesla adjustments. Formerly 'Long Range AWD' — Tesla renamed it 'Premium' in 2026 and raised the price $1,000 (May 2026). Battery size and 10–80% time are not published by Tesla; values are estimates.

vehicles.capability_note: Trunk figure includes the deep under-floor well; Tesla's 24 cu ft headline adds the 3.1 cu ft frunk. No official seats-folded figure. Not rated for towing in the US. Sub-trunk: included in the 21.0 cu ft (594 L) trunk figure. No separate official volume (aftermarket measurements give only dimensions).
vehicles.notes: Efficient sedan, strong Supercharger network. Formerly 'Long Range RWD' (renamed 'Premium' in 2026). A cheaper Model 3 Standard is also in the catalog.

vehicles.capability_note: No frunk. 1,500 lb tow rating when equipped with trailering provisions. Sub-trunk: reviews (Edmunds cargo test, dealer guides, via search excerpts) describe an under-floor bin sized for the charge-cord case and small items. Chevrolet publishes no separate volume, and it is unclear whether 26.4 cu ft includes it.
vehicles.notes: Most compelling mid-priced BEV SUV for WV market. Native NACS port from MY2027. Earlier data wrongly listed Ingersoll, Ontario assembly and understated energy use.

vehicles.capability_note: 5.5-ft bed (67.1 in at floor). 7,700 lb needs Max Trailer Tow Pkg (5,000 without). Payload is the XLT figure from dealer sources; Ford sheet lists 2,329 lb max for standard range (Pro). Pickup: sub-trunk set to 0. No under-bed or gear-tunnel storage; the 14.1 cu ft lockable frunk is the hidden storage (bed volume about 52.8 cu ft per review excerpt).
vehicles.notes: Pickup is the top-selling body style in WV. Home-backup power feature is a real selling point.
vehicles.status_note: Ford cancelled the battery-electric Lightning in Dec 2025 (an extended-range successor is planned). Leftover/used only; price shown is the last new MSRP.

vehicles.capability_note: 10,000 lb with Max Trailer Tow Pkg per dealer sources (7,700 without). Ford's 2025 spec sheet lists the extended-range battery only on Flash/Lariat/Platinum, so XLT ER may be a 2024 carry-over config. Pickup: sub-trunk set to 0. No under-bed or gear-tunnel storage; the 14.1 cu ft frunk is the hidden storage.
vehicles.notes: Extended Range battery (131 kWh) — 320 mi EPA. ~$15k more than Standard Range but real-world WV highway range jumps to ~245 mi. Better fit for long trips.
vehicles.status_note: Ford cancelled the battery-electric Lightning in Dec 2025 (an extended-range successor is planned). Leftover/used only; price shown is the last new MSRP.

vehicles.capability_note: 5 ft 11 in bed (nominal; extends with Multi-Flex Midgate). eTrunk 10.7 cu ft. Figures for LT Extended Range; payload varies by configuration. Pickup: sub-trunk set to 0. No under-bed storage found (bed about 57.7 cu ft per dealer comparison); only small in-cab bins behind the rear seat backs.
vehicles.notes: Extended Range — 410 mi EPA (InsideEVs 70-mph test on the 2025 LT Extended Range: 310 mi). Strong for contractors / fleet use in WV. MY2027 (production from Oct 2026) switches to a native NACS port and adds ~$200–400. The cheaper WT Standard Range is now in the catalog as a trim of this card. Towing is the Extended Range rating from GM Fleet and dealer specs (12,500 lb; the April figure of 10,000 lb was too low). Battery size is an estimate.

vehicles.capability_note: Assumes Standard battery pack. Plus 11.7 cu ft gear tunnel. Payload per Rivian support; 7,700 lb Standard-pack tow rating not re-confirmed for MY2027. Weight-distributing hitch needed above 5,000 lb. Pickup: sub-trunk set to 0. Besides the 11.7 cu ft gear tunnel there is a sealed under-bed compartment (spare-tire well with drain plug), reported as 11.5-14.3 cu ft by review sources (search excerpts).
vehicles.notes: Premium adventure truck. Limited WV dealer presence. AALA-exempt (GVWR >8,500 lbs — heavy vehicles not required to disclose parts content). Rivian dropped the 'Dual Standard' LFP pack for MY2027; Premium (old Large pack) is now the entry trim. Range on standard 20-inch wheels. Battery and charge time approximate. Peak DC kW for MY2027 not published; the figure shown carries over from 2026.

vehicles.capability_note: Large pack. Plus 11.7 cu ft gear tunnel. 11,000 lb needs weight-distributing hitch (5,000 without). MY2026 figures. Pickup: sub-trunk set to 0. Besides the 11.7 cu ft gear tunnel there is a sealed under-bed compartment (spare-tire well), reported as 11.5-14.3 cu ft by review sources.
vehicles.notes: Largest pack option — ~140 kWh / 380 mi EPA (20-inch wheels). AALA-exempt (GVWR >8,500 lbs). $7k step up from Premium for meaningful extra range. Old 'Max' pack, renamed Premium Long Range for MY2027. Battery approximate.

vehicles.capability_note: Frunk is a paid option (not standard) on 2026 per Ford order guide. Not rated for towing in the US per review sources (no tow package in 2026 order guide). CORRECTION: frunk changed from 4.7 to 2.6 cu ft. 4.7 was the pre-2025 frunk; the 2025 heat pump shrank it to 2.6 cu ft (Ford Authority, Electrek). Sub-trunk: small hidden under-floor bin for cables and valuables; reviews say it does not add meaningful luggage space. No published volume.
vehicles.notes: Established Ford dealer network in WV makes service convenient.

vehicles.capability_note: Frunk is optional on 2026. Not rated for towing in the US per review sources. CORRECTION: frunk changed from 4.7 to 2.6 cu ft (2025+ heat-pump frunk, per Ford Authority/Electrek). Sub-trunk: small under-floor bin, no published volume.
vehicles.notes: Premium with Extended Range 91 kWh pack — 320 mi EPA. Meaningful step up from Select Standard Range for WV drivers who regularly do longer trips. MSRP is approximate (Premium $40,595 + Extended Range option ~$5,245); confirm on ford.com.

vehicles.capability_note: Sources conflict: 26.3/58.5 (2025+ refresh) vs older 27.2/59.3. Frunk 0.85 cu ft. Hyundai lists 2,700 lb towing only for XRT; rating for SE not confirmed. Sub-trunk: reviews mention only small under-floor/side pockets; no published volume. Unclear whether Hyundai's figure includes them.
vehicles.notes: Class-leading DCFC speed. Assembled in Georgia (Metaplant opened 2024). Hyundai cut Ioniq 5 prices ~$9k for MY2026 after the federal credit ended (+$250 for MY2027).

vehicles.capability_note: Sources conflict: 26.3/58.5 vs 27.2/59.3. Frunk 0.85 cu ft. Towing rating for SE RWD not confirmed (XRT: 2,700 lb). Sub-trunk: only small under-floor pockets per reviews; no published volume.
vehicles.notes: Long Range 84 kWh pack — 318 mi EPA. Same 800V ultra-fast DCFC. Common step-up trim for WV buyers who want highway range without Tesla pricing. Hyundai cut Ioniq 5 prices ~$9k for MY2026. Hyundai publishes 10–80% in ~20 min but no peak kW; the 235 kW figure is from independent tests of earlier models.

vehicles.capability_note: Kia lists towing only for Long Range trims (2,700 lb); Light (standard range) has none. Frunk 1.8 cu ft (52 L, RWD) is from a non-US spec. Sub-trunk: multi-level under-floor storage (lift-up flap plus space under the floor, per What Car/Autoblog via search excerpts). No published volume; unclear whether 24.4 cu ft includes it.
vehicles.notes: Shares 800V platform with Ioniq 5. Fast DCFC. Highest US/CA parts content of any EV on this list (MY2025 AALA). Kia cut EV6 prices ~$5k for MY2026. US/Canadian parts % is the MY2025 figure.

vehicles.capability_note: 2,700 lb with trailer brakes. Frunk 1.8 cu ft (52 L, RWD) is from a non-US spec. Sub-trunk: under-floor storage present per reviews; no published volume.
vehicles.notes: Wind trim with 84 kWh Long Range pack — 319 mi EPA. Same 800V platform as Ioniq 5 LR. Topped the 2025 AALA index at 80% US/CA parts. Light Long Range RWD ($41,200) is a cheaper way to get the 84 kWh pack. US/Canadian parts % is the MY2025 figure.

vehicles.capability_note: 20 cu ft seats-up from Nissan; 55.5 folded from review sources. No frunk. No US tow rating found (1,300 lb figures appear to be non-US). Sub-trunk: no information found on an under-floor bin in the new-generation Leaf; left null (unknown).
vehicles.notes: All-new 3rd-gen Leaf on Nissan's AmpR Medium platform (shared with Ariya), now a crossover SUV rather than a hatchback. 75 kWh pack, 303 mi EPA, native NACS DCFC at 150 kW. MY2025 was the outgoing 40 kWh / 149 mi / CHAdeMO 2nd-gen carryover; this row reflects the fall-2025 3rd-gen that dealers are actually selling. Japan-built. One of the cheapest new EVs (with the Chevy Bolt). The cheaper 52 kWh 'S' trim was cancelled/delayed; S+ charges at 7.2 kW at home (higher trims may differ).

vehicles.capability_note: No frunk. 1,500 lb with trailering provisions (FWD LT); some AWD/RWD trims rate higher. Sub-trunk: no Blazer-specific figure found. The Ultium-platform sibling Honda Prologue has a 0.8 cu ft under-floor bin, but the Blazer's was not confirmed.
vehicles.notes: Larger, more traditional SUV format. 2LT trim no longer offered; LT FWD is the closest equivalent. Native NACS from MY2027.

vehicles.capability_note: No frunk. RWD 2,200 lb braked with VW hitch (AWD 2,700); some sources say RWD is not rated. Sub-trunk: two-level load floor with a small under-floor area (charge cord) below; the floor drops a level for more space. No published volume, and it is unclear which floor position the 30.3 cu ft figure uses.
vehicles.notes: Assembled in Tennessee. The 62 kWh Standard trim was dropped; Pro RWD is now the entry trim. US/Canadian parts % is the MY2025 figure.
vehicles.status_note: Chattanooga production ended April 2026; MY2026 dealer inventory expected into 2027.

vehicles.capability_note: No frunk. RWD 2,200 lb braked with VW hitch; some sources say RWD is not rated. Sub-trunk: two-level floor with a small under-floor area; no published volume, and it is unclear whether 30.3 includes it.
vehicles.notes: Pro S trim with 82 kWh larger battery — 291 mi EPA. TN-assembled. 3 yrs Electrify America included.
vehicles.status_note: Chattanooga production ended April 2026; MY2026 dealer inventory expected into 2027.

vehicles.capability_note: No frunk. 1,500 lb max towing. Honda spec page blocked direct fetch; figures from search excerpts. Sub-trunk: 0.8 cu ft bin under the trunk floor, described as 'separate' storage (Edmunds review via search excerpt), so treated as not included in 25.2 (inference).
vehicles.notes: GM platform under Honda skin. Strong Honda dealer network in WV. Assembled in Mexico despite Honda branding. Honda cut MSRP $7,500 in April 2026 but reduced dealer cash by about the same amount, so real transaction prices barely moved.
vehicles.status_note: Honda ends Prologue sales after MY2026; no Honda EV is planned for the US in 2027.

vehicles.capability_note: MY2026 figures. No frunk. XLE FWD Plus listed without a tow rating (3,500 lb is on Woodland/AWD grades). Sub-trunk: reviews (Capital One Auto Navigator, dealer, via search excerpts) describe a large under-floor bin used for the charge cord. No published volume; unclear whether 27.7 includes it.
vehicles.notes: Toyota reliability reputation. Manufactured in Japan. Renamed from bZ4X to bZ for 2026 with a larger battery and NACS port. AWD XLE is $39,900 / 288 mi; base XLE FWD (57.7 kWh) is $34,980 / 236 mi.

vehicles.capability_note: New-generation 2026 model; seats-folded figure not found. 3,500 lb tow rating. Sub-trunk: 2026 RAV4 has a height-adjustable deck board (about 2 in lower position) with storage beneath; no published volume for the plug-in, and unclear which position the 33.5 figure uses.
vehicles.notes: Excellent WV option: ~52 mi electric covers most commutes, gas backup eliminates range anxiety. Assembled in Japan. New-generation replacement for the RAV4 Prime. Electric range (52 mi; some sources say 54 for SE) and hybrid-mode mpg (40) are Toyota projections — not yet EPA-listed. Total range uses Toyota's '490+ mi' (other sources claim 550–600). SE charges at 7 kW with no DC fast charging (XSE/Woodland get 11 kW and CCS).

vehicles.capability_note: Escape is being discontinued; figures match 2025. Rear seat slides, so behind-row-2 space varies. Sub-trunk: no information found on an under-floor bin for the PHEV; left null (unknown).
vehicles.notes: Ford dealer ubiquity in WV. Final model year, single trim ($35,400 + $1,495 destination).
vehicles.status_note: Production ended Dec 2025. Leftover dealer stock only.

vehicles.capability_note: Stellantis 2025 spec sheet, 4-door Sport S 4xe. Sub-trunk: owner forums describe a factory under-floor bin in the rear cargo area (4xe keeps it, with a raised floor over the battery). No published volume; unclear whether 27.7 includes it.
vehicles.notes: Off-road capable with electric assist. Popular body style in WV; shorter EV-only range. Previous data listed 49 kWh/100mi — that was the MPGe figure, not kWh. EPA electric-mode use is 68 kWh/100mi.
vehicles.status_note: Stellantis ended all North American plug-in hybrids in Jan 2026. Used market only.

vehicles.capability_note: Sedan trunk. No US tow rating found. Frunk re-tried: all North American 2023-2025 Ioniq 6 (RWD and AWD) get the shallow 15 L (0.5 cu ft) frunk tray; the 45 L deep tub is non-US RWD only (Go-Parts, The Autopian, via search excerpts). Sub-trunk: no information found on an under-floor bin; left null (unknown).
vehicles.notes: Most efficient non-Tesla EV. Aerodynamic sedan shape. Assembled in South Korea — 0% US/CA content.
vehicles.status_note: Hyundai dropped the regular Ioniq 6 from the US for MY2026 (only the ~$70k Ioniq 6 N remains). Used market only.

vehicles.capability_note: Volvo says the folded figure includes a 2.2 cu ft under-floor compartment. Tiny 0.2 cu ft frunk. 2,000 lb towing from review sources. Sub-trunk: 2.2 cu ft under-floor compartment. Sources say the 27.8 folded figure includes it but do not say so for the 12.4 seats-up figure, so treated as excluded (inference).
vehicles.notes: Small premium crossover. US production moved from China to Belgium for MY2026 and the price dropped ~$6k; the 'Core' trim is gone.
vehicles.status_note: Volvo is ending US EX30 sales in 2026 (dealer order cutoff March 2026); remaining inventory only.

vehicles.capability_note: Cargo verified on Kia media spec page; frunk 0.7 cu ft is from non-official sources. Kia lists no towing rating. Sub-trunk: dual-level cargo floor with an under-floor compartment (charge cable, tools) per reviews. No published volume; unclear whether 22.8 is measured with the floor lowered.
vehicles.notes: Practical, reliable. Slower DCFC than Kia EV6. Assembled in South Korea.
vehicles.status_note: MY2026 is the Niro EV's final model year; dealer inventory only.

vehicles.capability_note: 7-seat. Behind-row-2 figure is with 3rd row folded. Frunk 3.2 cu ft (RWD). 2,000 lb braked towing for Light Long Range RWD. Sub-trunk: 0. Reviews (Autoblog luggage test, via search excerpt) say the under-floor space only holds the cargo cover and tire-repair kit, with no useful luggage bin.
vehicles.notes: Flagship 3-row family EV. US-assembled since late 2024. Biggest recent addition to the family-SUV EV segment. Previously listed as 'Wind RWD', which doesn't exist; the specs match Light Long Range RWD. Kia has been running ~$10k customer cash on the EV9.

vehicles.capability_note: No frunk. Max cargo reported as about 60 cu ft (exact Cadillac figure not confirmed). 3,500 lb with trailering package. Sub-trunk: reviews describe a deep under-floor storage area, larger than in rivals, plus a slot for the charge-cord case. No published volume; unclear whether 28.0 includes it.
vehicles.notes: Premium US-assembled EV on GM platform. GM dealer network broad in WV.

vehicles.capability_note: MY2026 figures (same generation). Hatchback. No tow rating listed. Sub-trunk: not researched in depth; no information found. Left null (unknown).
vehicles.notes: Benchmark PHEV efficiency — ~51 mpg on gas, 44 mi all-electric. Japan-assembled. Renamed from Prius Prime. Efficiency figures are MY2025 EPA; MY2027 EPA listing pending.

vehicles.capability_note: MY2026 figures from Subaru's trim-comparison PDF. No frunk. Tow rating is not in Subaru's spec sheet (one source claims 3,500 lb, unconfirmed). Sub-trunk: modest cargo-area under-floor storage tray (dealer/review excerpts). No published volume; unclear whether 23.8 includes it.
vehicles.notes: Badge-engineered twin of the Toyota bZ (formerly bZ4X) with Subaru AWD. Strong Subaru dealer presence in WV. Japan-assembled. Larger 74.7 kWh battery and NACS port from MY2026. Standard AWD.

vehicles.capability_note: Liftback trunk; seats-folded figure not found. No frunk. US tow rating not found. Sub-trunk: small under-floor compartments (cables). i4 owner forum/review excerpts say the 470 L (16.6 cu ft) figure excludes under-floor storage. No volume published.
vehicles.notes: Entry-luxury BMW EV sedan. Germany-built. Earlier data used the discontinued eDrive35's $52,200 price; eDrive40 is $57,900.

vehicles.capability_note: Liftback. Frunk 1.2 cu ft. 2,000 lb towing. Sub-trunk: about 41 L (1.4 cu ft) under the double load floor (Motor1/DrivingElectric via search excerpts; frunk is separately about 35 L). Sources don't make clear whether the 405 L (14.3-14.4 cu ft) trunk figure includes the under-floor 41 L.
vehicles.notes: Volvo/Geely sub-brand. China-assembled — no IRA credit and subject to import tariffs.
vehicles.status_note: Withdrawn from the US (tariffs and the connected-vehicle rule bar MY2027+). Used market only.

vehicles.capability_note: 6 ft x 4 ft bed (72 in nominal). 11,000 lb towing and 2,500 lb payload for AWD. Frunk re-tried: 7.1 cu ft (about 200 L), 420 lb load limit, per Not a Tesla App / Tesloid (search excerpts). Pickup: sub-trunk set to 0. There is a 3.4 cu ft (97 L) under-bed compartment with drain plug (owner's manual via search excerpt); bed ('vault') is about 67 cu ft.
vehicles.notes: Polarizing design but high mindshare. Highway range derated further than Model Y/3 due to massive frontal area. A cheaper Dual Motor AWD trim ($69,990, same EPA range) launched in 2026. 10–80% time is a third-party estimate.

vehicles.capability_note: No frunk. 7,200 lb with factory trailer hitch. Sub-trunk: no information found on under-floor storage in the PHEV (battery raises the floor vs the gas X5). Left null (unknown).
vehicles.notes: Popular luxury PHEV. 40 mi electric covers most commutes. SC-assembled. MY2026 EPA figures; MSRP approximate. A new-generation 2027 X5 50e xDrive ($77,500, ~44 mi electric est.) arrives October 2026.

vehicles.capability_note: Rivian spec: 17.6 cu ft all seats up, 48.6 third row folded, 90.7 second+third folded; frunk 9.9 cu ft (Rivian page; older sources say 11.1). 7,700 lb requires weight-distributing hitch (5,000 lb without). Page is current Gen 2 R1S, not explicitly MY2027. Sub-trunk: R1S has an under-floor bin behind the 3rd row but Rivian gives no separate volume (its 105.8 cu ft 'total storage' implies ~5 cu ft of under-floor + cubby space beyond frunk + 90.7). Unknown whether 48.6 includes it.
vehicles.notes: 3-row SUV sibling of R1T. AALA-exempt (GVWR >8,500 lbs). Rivian dropped the 'Dual Standard' LFP pack for MY2027; Premium is now the entry trim. Battery and charge time approximate. Peak DC kW for MY2027 not published; the figure shown carries over from 2026.

vehicles.capability_note: Rivian spec: 17.6 cu ft all seats up, 48.6 third row folded, 90.7 second+third folded; frunk 9.9 cu ft (Rivian page; older sources say 11.1). 7,700 lb requires weight-distributing hitch (5,000 lb without). Page is current Gen 2 R1S, not explicitly MY2027. All Gen 2 R1S battery/motor combos rated 7,700 lb. Sub-trunk: R1S has an under-floor bin behind the 3rd row but Rivian gives no separate volume (its 105.8 cu ft 'total storage' implies ~5 cu ft of under-floor + cubby space beyond frunk + 90.7). Unknown whether 48.6 includes it.
vehicles.notes: Large pack variant — 135 kWh / 352 mi EPA. AALA-exempt. $5k step up for meaningful extra range on long trips.

vehicles.capability_note: MBUSA 2025 EQB 250+: 25.9-61.8 cu ft; 5 seats std, 3rd row optional. EQB 250+ is FWD (batch trim says 4MATIC). MBUSA lists no US towing capacity (European rating ~3,100 lb braked); left null. Sub-trunk: no data; unknown.
vehicles.notes: Entry-luxury Mercedes EV SUV. Compact platform, 5-seat. Hungary-assembled — no IRA credit. Slowest DCFC of the Mercedes lineup (100 kW peak).
vehicles.status_note: Discontinued in the US after MY2025. Used market only. The new electric CLA is Mercedes' entry EV.

vehicles.capability_note: MBUSA MY2026 EQE 320 4MATIC Sedan lists 10.9 cu ft trunk (older reviews quote ~15 cu ft for earlier EQE 350). No frunk. MBUSA lists no towing capacity for the sedan. Sub-trunk: no data.
vehicles.notes: Mid-tier Mercedes executive EV sedan. Germany-assembled — no IRA credit.
vehicles.status_note: MY2026 is the final model year for the EQE sedan.

vehicles.capability_note: MBUSA MY2027 EQE 320 4MATIC SUV: 14-55 cu ft (Mercedes' conservative measure; European VDA figures are 520/1,675 L = 18.4/59.2 cu ft). 3,500 lb with optional trailer hitch. No frunk. Sub-trunk: EQE SUV has an under-floor compartment for cables/first-aid kit; size not published.
vehicles.notes: US-assembled at Mercedes' Tuscaloosa plant. Popular mid-size luxury SUV. EPA-listed for MY2027, though some reports say EQE production ends in 2026 — confirm availability with a dealer.

charging.connector_dcfc: CCS (Tesla Supercharger access via NACS adapter)

vehicles.capability_note: Lucid tech specs (MY2024/2025): trunk 22.1 cu ft, frunk 10.0 cu ft; towing listed as not available. No official seats-folded figure. MY2027 same generation. Sub-trunk: 22.1 cu ft trunk figure includes the deep under-floor well (size not given separately).
vehicles.notes: EPA range champion of the US market at 512 mi (19-inch wheels). 21-inch wheels drop to 446 mi. Class-leading 19.2 kW onboard charger. Tesla Supercharger access opened in 2024 via Lucid-provided NACS adapter. Used-market relevance: early Air GT depreciation has been steep.

vehicles.capability_note: MY2027 Grand Touring seats 5 standard; 7-seat 3rd row is a $2,900 option (then 21.3 cu ft behind 3rd row, 106.2 max). Cargo figures from review summaries (56.2 behind 2nd, 111.9 max in 2-row config); Lucid quotes 'up to 120 cu ft' incl. frunk. 6,000 lb requires optional $950 Towing Package. Sub-trunk: size not found.
vehicles.notes: Lucid's first SUV; 3-row seating with optional 6-seat captain's chairs. 400 kW peak DCFC is class-leading — adds ~200 mi in 11 min on a 350 kW+ charger. Native NACS DCFC port, so Superchargers are plug-and-charge. Rare in WV dealer inventory; most sales online-direct.

vehicles.capability_note: MBUSA MY2027 EQS 450+ Sedan: 22-63 cu ft (liftback, so a seats-folded figure exists). No frunk. MBUSA lists no towing capacity. Sub-trunk: no data.
vehicles.notes: Mercedes flagship luxury sedan — 390 mi EPA (MY2026), one of the longest-range German EVs sold in the US. German-assembled. Used-market shoppers: early EQS (2022-2023) depreciated heavily, strong used-buyer value. Refreshed for 2027 (800-volt, 122 kWh). Range and efficiency shown are MY2026 EPA values; MY2027 ratings pending.

vehicles.capability_note: Tesla quotes 28 cu ft total incl. frunk; split per Tesla EU data: rear 709 L (25.0 cu ft, includes sub-trunk) + frunk 89 L (3.1). Seats-folded 64.6 cu ft is an EU litre conversion. Tesla offers no tow hitch for Model S in North America (towing not supported). Sub-trunk: Model S has a deep rear sub-trunk; not published separately but included in the 25.0.
vehicles.notes: Tesla flagship sedan, 410 mi EPA. MY2026 price cut to $74,990 before Tesla ceased Model S/X production in April 2026 — dealer and used-market inventory remains active. Highway range in practice typically 290–320 mi (Tesla EPA is known to overstate; WV elevation and cold compound this). Supercharger network access is the main practical advantage.
vehicles.status_note: Production ended May 2026. Used market only; price shown is the last new MSRP.

vehicles.capability_note: 30.2 behind 2nd row (measured with floor panel removed, i.e. includes sub-trunk; China MIIT 854 L), 72.1 max, 4.1 frunk: pre-refresh figures; Tesla quotes 76 cu ft total for current Model Y. 3,500 lb requires Tesla tow hitch option. Sub-trunk: large rear under-floor well included in 30.2; separate volume not published.
vehicles.notes: Model Y Performance — 3.3s 0-60, uprated brakes, lowered suspension, 21-inch wheels. Range drops ~25 mi vs LR due to wheels/motor. Updated for the 2026 new-body Model Y Performance ($57,990 after a $500 increase in May 2026; 306 mi EPA). Battery size and charge time are unconfirmed estimates.

vehicles.capability_note: Tesla quotes 24 cu ft total incl. frunk; EU data: rear ~594 L (21 cu ft, includes sub-trunk) + frunk 88 L (3.1). Seats-folded ~43.6 cu ft (EU litre conversion) not officially quoted in US. Tesla owner's manual: Model 3 not approved for towing in North America. Sub-trunk: rear under-floor well included in trunk figure; separate volume not published.
vehicles.notes: Model 3 Performance — 2.9s 0-60, track-tuned suspension, adaptive dampers. Fastest sub-$60k EV sedan on the market. MY2027 EPA figures (316 mi); price unchanged at $54,990. Battery size is unconfirmed.

vehicles.capability_note: Rivian: bed 54.1 in (tailgate up), payload 1,764 lb and towing 11,000 lb for R1T Dual (Max pack); Gen 2 Dual Standard/Large pack rated 7,700 lb. Weight-distributing hitch required for max. Frunk 9.9 cu ft per Rivian page. Sub-trunk 0: pickup - the 11.7 cu ft gear tunnel and under-bed storage are not a sub-trunk.
vehicles.notes: Dual-motor Performance (now the Premium trim's $5,000 power upgrade) — 665 hp, 3.4s 0-60, same tow/payload as Standard. For MY2027 the standard pack is ~108.5 kWh usable (300 mi EPA on 20-inch wheels); the Long Range pack (~140 kWh, 380 mi) is an upgrade. Rivian renamed trims for MY2027: its new 'Performance' trim is the former tri-motor (~$101k), not this dual-motor version. Price = Premium + $5,000 power upgrade; destination extra.

vehicles.capability_note: Rivian spec: 17.6 cu ft all seats up, 48.6 third row folded, 90.7 second+third folded; frunk 9.9 cu ft (Rivian page; older sources say 11.1). 7,700 lb requires weight-distributing hitch (5,000 lb without). Page is current Gen 2 R1S, not explicitly MY2027. Sub-trunk: R1S has an under-floor bin behind the 3rd row but Rivian gives no separate volume (its 105.8 cu ft 'total storage' implies ~5 cu ft of under-floor + cubby space beyond frunk + 90.7). Unknown whether 48.6 includes it.
vehicles.notes: Dual-motor Performance (now the Premium trim's $5,000 power upgrade) — 665 hp, 3.4s 0-60 for a 3-row full-size SUV. For MY2027 the standard pack is ~108.5 kWh usable (300 mi EPA on 20-inch wheels); the Long Range pack (~140 kWh, 380 mi) is an upgrade. Rivian renamed trims for MY2027: its new 'Performance' trim is the former tri-motor (~$101k), not this dual-motor version. Price = Premium + $5,000 power upgrade; destination extra.

vehicles.capability_note: Dealer research page (Cadillac figures): 23.6 behind 3rd, 69.1 behind 2nd, 119.1 behind 1st row. eTrunk 12.2 cu ft. Max trailering 8,000 lb (IQ; IQL is 7,500) per review/dealer sources. Sub-trunk: no data.
vehicles.notes: Cadillac flagship EV — 200 kWh battery (largest in class), ~460 mi range (Cadillac estimate), 750 hp in Velocity Max launch mode. Same Detroit plant as Silverado EV. Not EPA-labeled (too heavy), so range and efficiency are manufacturer/third-party figures. MSRP approximate ($130,300 including destination). MY2027 adds a native NACS port.

vehicles.capability_note: Nissan USA: up to 59.7 cu ft max; 22.8 behind rear seats per review/dealer sources. No frunk. Nissan lists towing (1,500 lb) only for e-4ORCE AWD; FWD Evolve+ has no published rating - null. Sub-trunk: no data.
vehicles.notes: Nissan mid-size EV crossover, 87 kWh long-range pack. Slow home-charging (7.2 kW) — plan for overnight. Japan-built. Trim corrected (there is no 'SV' Ariya; the 87 kWh FWD trim is Evolve+).
vehicles.status_note: Nissan dropped the Ariya from the US for MY2026. Used/leftover only; price shown is the last new MSRP.

vehicles.capability_note: Bed 70.6 in (10 ft 10 in with MultiPro Midgate down). 12,500 lb max trailering. Payload conflicts: 1,950 lb (review summary for Denali Extended Range) vs 2,250 lb (dealer page, Denali 4WD). eTrunk 11.0 cu ft per dealer (another source said 15; Silverado EV's is 10.7). Sub-trunk 0 (pickup).
vehicles.notes: Silverado EV twin with Denali trim — premium interior, same ~170 kWh Extended Range pack, 410 mi EPA. Corrected: the 205 kWh pack is the Max Range version (~478 mi, ~$101k). Highway range matches the mechanically identical Silverado EV Extended Range. MSRP approximate ($80,495 including destination). MY2027 adds NACS.

vehicles.capability_note: Acura MY2024 spec release (read via search excerpt): 29.7 / 63.0 cu ft. 3,500 lb requires Acura accessory trailer hitch. No frunk. Sub-trunk: no data.
vehicles.notes: Acura's first EV, built on GM Ultium at Spring Hill alongside Cadillac Lyriq and Honda Prologue. Only MY2024 was sold (the id says 2025 but is kept so shared links work). 10–80% figure is Acura's 20–80% time.
vehicles.status_note: Acura ended ZDX production in September 2025. Used market only; price shown is the 2024 launch MSRP.

vehicles.capability_note: Liftback coupe: 22.8 cu ft behind rear seat, 37.4 folded (dealer/review figures quoting Dodge spec sheet; Edmunds cites 22.7). Frunk 1.5 cu ft only with optional Plus Group - 0 as standard. Towing not found. Sub-trunk: no data.
vehicles.notes: Stellantis electric muscle car — retuned Fratzonic exhaust audio, 496 hp R/T dual motor AWD. Canada-assembled. EPA range is for 18-inch wheels (308 mi on 20-inch). Battery is usable capacity.
vehicles.status_note: Dodge dropped the R/T after MY2025; only leftover R/Ts remain. MY2027 is Scat Pack only ($72,495).

vehicles.capability_note: 16.2 behind 2nd row, 56.3 folded (dealer/review summaries of GM figures). Frunk not confirmed either way (re-tried). No published tow rating found. Sub-trunk: no data.
vehicles.notes: Returns for 2027 with an LFP battery and native NACS. Cheapest new EV in the catalog ($28,995 with destination). City/highway split derived from EPA MPGe.

vehicles.capability_note: Kia US spec: 26.1 / 56.5 cu ft with cargo floor at lowest level; front trunk 0.88 cu ft. No towing capacity listed. Sub-trunk: Kia's figure is measured with the cargo floor at its lowest level, so it includes the under-floor space; separate size not published.
vehicles.notes: Priced August 2026. Light FWD ($29,890, 221 mi) and Wind AWD ($38,690, 280 mi) also offered. US-market EV3s are built in Mexico (production started Aug 2026; the earliest units may be Korean-built). Peak DC ~128 kW is the European spec; Kia US publishes only 10–80% times.

vehicles.capability_note: Same body as other Model Y: 30.2 (incl. sub-trunk) / 72.1 / 4.1 frunk, pre-refresh figures; Tesla quotes 76 cu ft total. 3,500 lb with tow hitch option per third-party listing - confirm Standard trim offers the hitch. Sub-trunk: included in 30.2; separate volume not published.
vehicles.notes: Cheaper, de-contented Model Y (late 2025). Standard AWD is $41,990 / 294 mi. Battery (~69.5 kWh usable) and 7.7 kW home charging are from press reviews; Tesla doesn't publish them. 10–80% time is an estimate.

vehicles.capability_note: EU data: trunk 593 L (20.9 cu ft, includes sub-trunk), frunk 88 L (3.1); Tesla US quotes ~24 cu ft total. Seats-folded 43.6 (EU) not quoted in US. Not approved for towing in North America per Tesla owner's manual. Sub-trunk: included in trunk figure; separate volume not published.
vehicles.notes: Cheaper Model 3 trim (late 2025). Tesla doesn't publish battery size or charge times: battery is assumed to match the Model Y Standard (same 321-mi EPA range and efficiency), and home charging (~7.7 kW) and 10–80% time are unconfirmed estimates.

vehicles.capability_note: GM MY2025 release: WT Standard Range up to 8,500 lb towing and 2,350 lb payload. 5 ft 11 in (70.7 in) bed; eTrunk 10.7 cu ft. MY2027 not confirmed. Sub-trunk 0 (pickup).
vehicles.notes: With the F-150 Lightning cancelled, this is the cheapest full-size electric pickup. EPA figures are MY2026 (2027 carries over). Towing (8,500 lb) and payload (2,350 lb) are GM Fleet's MY2026 WT Standard Range figures; 2027 ratings not yet published. Battery size is a third-party estimate; whether MSRP includes destination is unconfirmed; 10–80% time not published.

vehicles.capability_note: Toyota spec: 25.3 behind rear seat, 59.5 behind front seat (JBL-equipped figures). No frunk. Towing not listed on Toyota spec page. Sub-trunk: no data.
vehicles.notes: Standard AWD. Shares the 74.7 kWh battery with the bZ, Solterra, Trailseeker, and Uncharted. Not rated to tow.

vehicles.capability_note: Subaru spec: Premium/Limited 31.3 / 74.0 cu ft (Touring 30.4 / 71.8). No frunk. Towing 3,500 lb per Subaru launch info; not shown on the spec page. Sub-trunk: no data.
vehicles.notes: Wagon-style electric Subaru with standard AWD and a 3,500 lb tow rating — a natural fit for WV. 10–80% time approximate.

vehicles.capability_note: Subaru spec: 20.8 cu ft with deck board up / 23.0 with deck board in lower position. No max cargo or towing figure listed. No frunk. Sub-trunk: 2.2 cu ft = difference between deck-board lower and upper positions.
vehicles.notes: Compact electric Subaru. Premium FWD is $34,995 / 308 mi. Not rated to tow.

vehicles.capability_note: Hyundai spec: 86.9 / 46.7 / 21.9 cu ft behind 1st/2nd/3rd row; SE AWD 7 seats, 5,000 lb with trailer brakes (RWD S: 3,500). Frunk volume not listed on Hyundai US spec page. Sub-trunk: no data. Frunk re-tried; still not found.
vehicles.notes: Three-row electric SUV. There is no plug-in minivan on the US market anymore; this and the Kia EV9 are the closest family haulers. Peak DC 233 kW and 10.9 kW home charging per Hyundai spec and US reports.

vehicles.capability_note: MBUSA (MY2027 CLA 250+ page): 1.4 cu ft front / 10.3 cu ft rear. Towing only 'with optional trailer hitch', no capacity shown - null. Sub-trunk: no data.
vehicles.notes: Mercedes' new entry EV, effectively replacing the EQB. 374 mi is the best-case configuration.

vehicles.capability_note: Rivian: rear cargo 28.7, seats folded 79.4, 'total storage' 90.1 cu ft; 4,400 lb with Tow Package (included in Launch Package); payload 1,168 lb. Frunk 5.2 cu ft per Wikipedia (not on Rivian page). Sub-trunk: unknown; 90.1 'total storage' minus 79.4 leaves ~10.7 cu ft for frunk plus other bins.
vehicles.notes: Deliveries began spring 2026 with the launch edition. Cheaper trims follow: Premium ~$53,990 (late 2026), Standard ~$44,990–48,490 (2027). Home charging rate (~11.5 kW) is unconfirmed.

vehicles.capability_note: Hyundai spec: 31.9 seats up; 66.3 SAE seats folded (71.8 by Hyundai 'max' method). 2,000 lb with trailer brakes (1,650 without). Sub-trunk: no data.
vehicles.notes: Standard AWD. MSRP approximate (sources vary $40,325–40,825).

vehicles.capability_note: Kia spec (SAE, dual-level floor lowest position): 34.5 / 65.5 cu ft. 2,000 lb braked / 1,653 unbraked; requires additional equipment. Sub-trunk: figure is measured with the dual-level floor in its lowest position, so under-floor space is included; separate size not published.
vehicles.notes: Standard AWD. Whether MSRP includes destination is unconfirmed.

vehicles.capability_note: Kia spec: behind 1st/2nd/3rd row 75.5 / 38.5-45.0 / 12.6 cu ft (2nd-row figure varies with seat slide; lower value used). EX is 7-passenger (6 with Premium Package). 2,000 lb towing. Sub-trunk: has a dual-level cargo floor; size and whether it is in the SAE figure not stated.
vehicles.notes: Three-row plug-in hybrid. Seat count, cargo, and towing unconfirmed.

vehicles.capability_note: Mitsubishi spec (with sunroof): 30.8 behind 2nd row, 64.7 behind front seats; behind-3rd-row figure not listed. 7 seats std; 1,500 lb max towing. Sub-trunk: no data.
vehicles.notes: The only 7-seat plug-in hybrid under ~$45k. Charges slowly at home (3.3 kW, ~6.5 hours on Level 2). DC fast charging uses CHAdeMO, which few US stations still support.
